title: Ночёвка с Родионом Сергеевичем  (Sleeping Over with Rodion Sergeyevich)

segments.t: Back at the apartment, Kostya is outraged to discover that Rodion Sergeyevich has been using his expensive face cream in the bathroom. Worse still, when Rodion climbs into bed without underwear and snores like a freight train, neither Max nor Kostya can get a wink of sleep.
Жалко звука нет.
Максим, еще раз так скажешь, я обижусь.
И кто вам разрешил за ним следить?
И вообще, вы не имеете права.
Имеет право твой крем брать?
Блин, этот крем стоит...
Хотя, если ему надо, пусть берет.
А все потому.
Макс, слушай, я тебя как друга прошу, а?
Спокойной ночи, Максим Леонидович.
Кстати, ничего, что я без нижнего белья.
Я просто привык к свободе во всем.
Он так храпит.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Жалко звука нет.
'Too bad there is no sound.' In Russian, the idea of 'feel sorry for' flows naturally into 'there is no' without extra filler words.
Максим, еще раз так скажешь, я обижусь.
'Maxim, if you say that one more time, I will be offended.' Kostya brings out the contrast between 'Maxim' and 'else' in a few short words.
И кто вам разрешил за ним следить?
'And who gave you permission to spy on him?' Notice how Russian expresses 'both' and 'to watch' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
И вообще, вы не имеете права.
'Besides, you have no right to do that.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'both' and finishing on 'right'.
Имеет право твой крем брать?
'Does he have the right to use your face cream?' Notice how Russian expresses 'has' and 'to take' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Блин, этот крем стоит...
'Man, that cream costs a fortune...' The meaning hinges on 'damn' working together with 'costs' in spoken Russian. Max answers right away.
Хотя, если ему надо, пусть берет.
'Although if he needs it, let him use it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'at least' and 'takes' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
А все потому.
'And all because of that.' Kostya anchors the line on 'and', while 'because' completes the thought.
Макс, слушай, я тебя как друга прошу, а?
'Max, listen, I am begging you as a friend, okay?' In Russian, the idea of 'Max' flows naturally into 'and' without extra filler words. Max answers right away.
Спокойной ночи, Максим Леонидович.
'Good night, Maxim Leonidovich.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'peaceful' before landing on 'leonidovich'.
Кстати, ничего, что я без нижнего белья.
'By the way, I hope you do not mind that I sleep without underwear.' The grammar packs 'by the way' and 'linen' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Я просто привык к свободе во всем.
'I am simply accustomed to freedom in all things.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'to everyone'. Max answers right away.
Он так храпит.
'He snores so loudly.' Max brings out the contrast between 'he' and 'like this' in a few short words. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
